description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to contribute to the modernization of selected public hospital services and to support the reconstruction of selected medical facilities damaged by the 2019 earthquake.

The objectives of the Health System Improvement Project for Albania is to contribute to improving the efficiency of care in selected hospitals in Albania, improving the management of information in the health system, and increasing financial access to health services. The project is also directly aligned with the Government?s health sector reform strategy and will support the implementation of the Government?s reform agenda. To improve access and efficiency of health care services in Albania, the Project will support: a) reforming the hospital sector by creating a sound legal framework and management structure for efficient service provision, strengthening performance management and planning, overcoming operational constraints in service delivery, supporting rationalization of the hospital network, and strengthening the referral system; b) improving monitoring and management of service quality and efficiency through the establishment of a health management information system and of a medical equipment management and maintenance system; and c) reforming the health financing and provider payment systems, improving capacity of the HIF for strategic purchasing, strengthening systems for efficient purchasing/distribution of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, and assessing options to expand insurance coverage within the available fiscal space.

title.narrative: Number of people accessing the expanded health services provided at hospitals supported through the project

comment.narrative:
Achieved.
This WBG corporate results indicator (CRI) tracks people benefiting from inpatient and emergency outpatient services at all 11 regional hospitals and the QSUT (Annex 12) that benefited from improved services during the project. It corrects the baseline value of the CRI indicator that was incorrectly documented as the improved facilities had not yet been constructed or upgraded at the start of the project, and correct baseline should have been zero. The catchment area data, as provided, is presented in Annex 12. It is noted that, based on the updated catchment area figures, the resulting number of people benefiting slightly increases compared to what was reported in the final ISR: from 900 000 to 921,692. As such, the CRI achievement at project closing was 921,692 over a baseline of 0.

title.narrative: Number of facilities renovated and/or equipped

baseline.value: 11 regional hospitals received medical equipment. 3 main hospitals are under rehabilitation

target.value: 11 regional hospitals equipped; 4 regional and municipal hospitals renovated; 3 departments of QSUT renovated

comment.narrative:
Mostly achieved.
By June 2025, 11 hospitals have been equipped; renovations completed at 4 hospitals (Laci Kukes, Kruja, and Lezha). In addition, renovation is completed in the two QSUT Department Hospitals (Cardio-Surgery and Pediatric). Regarding the Psychiatric Hospital, works in the Children Psychiatry building have been succesfully completed, while a relatively small amount of works in the Emergency Psychiatry building may not be fully completed by the closing date.
All medical equipment has been delivered, installed, and tested, with the exception of a few additional pieces of equipment procured under a contract amendment for Lezha hospital (expected to be delivered and installed by September 19, 2025).

As noted above, RHIS is functional in all the 11 regional hospitals. Given the time lag for data collection, data is currently available for the first four hospitals, as follows: Shkoder 34%, Durres 27%, Elbasan 51%, and Vlore 39%. Since no data are available from the remaining seven hospitals that were added under AF the result will remain unchanged, and the status of the indicator will stay “mostly achieved.”

Overachieved.
11 regional hospitals, 22 municipal hospitals, and five university hospitals have been accredited.

Mostly achieved.
This is a World Bank corporate results indicator. It tracks the number of people or businesses who use new or enhanced digitally enabled services through support by the Project. This includes new digitally delivered services as well as enhancements to existing digitally delivered services (i.e., those delivered through digital technologies such as internet, cloud computing, AI, etc.). The target value is expected to be fully achieved by Project closing date. However, reporting on the achieved value is connected with the data collection for RHIS. Hence, the result will be reported in the Project ICR.

title.narrative: People receiving quality health, nutrition, and population services

comment.narrative:
Achieved.
This is a World Bank corporate results indicator. It tracks the number of people benefitting, directly and indirectly, from inpatient and emergency services at the 11 regional hospitals and the tertiary hospital (QSUT). These services include the full continuum of health prevention, promotion, curtive, rehabilitative and palliative care that is safe, effective, and patient-centered.
Baseline: 300,000 individuals benefiting from inpatient services + 600,000 individuals benefiting from emergency services with no more than 1 day in the hospital (2023, MoHSP).
Given the Project coverage (all 11 regional hospitals and QSUT), all the existing user population is expected to have sustained access to quality inpatient and emergency services.

It tracks the number of people benefitting, directly and indirectly, from inpatient and emergency services at the 11 regional hospitals and the tertiary hospital (QSUT). These services include the full continuum of health prevention, promotion, curtive, rehabilitative and palliative care that is safe, effective, and patient-centered.
